Diagnosis.Molecular Markers: ER+ (>90%), PR+ (50%), HER2 equivocal (IHC 2; FISH pending)

Additional Comments: The patient is a 33-year-old premenopausal woman with a recent diagnosis of hormone receptor-positive (HR+) metastatic breast cancer involving lymph nodes. She initially presented with a right lateral neck lump, which progressively increased in size and number, leading to further evaluation. Imaging studies revealed diffuse bilateral cervical adenopathy, multiple FDG-avid lymph nodes in the right cervical and axillary regions, and heterogeneous breast tissue with areas of FDG-avidity. A biopsy confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma consistent with a breast primary, with ER+ (>90%), PR+ (50%), and HER2 equivocal status. The patient has no other evidence of distant metastasis and is awaiting further biopsy results and HER2 FISH results to complete her workup and finalize her treatment plan.
